output.summary: A biennial or short-lived perennial flowering plant native to southern and western Europe as far north as northwestern France, it has spiny stems and leaves with bright yellow to orange-yellow flowerheads. Wild-harvested plants are eaten in regional Spanish dishes, while southern Italian leaves are traditionally gathered during Holy Week for an Easter meat pie.
output.edibilityNote: Young plants, including roots, were eaten raw or stewed in 16th-century Salamanca; wild plants and leaves remain used in regional Spanish and Italian dishes.
